changes.before: Create slots with required person/day columns and a composite primary key. Store Mira/Mon, Mira/Tue and Oren/Mon once each.
changes.after: Use two columns together to identify a row.

before: A composite key identifies a row by a combination. PRIMARY KEY(person,day) lets Mira appear on different days and lets different people share Monday. Only the whole pair must be unique. Explicit NOT NULL on both columns also rules out incomplete identities.

UNIQUE(person,day) likewise forbids repeating a complete non-NULL pair, but SQLite treats NULLs as distinct for uniqueness. Ordinary rowid tables have a legacy exception: a non-INTEGER PRIMARY KEY may also allow NULL unless NOT NULL is declared. STRICT tables and WITHOUT ROWID tables make primary-key columns required. In a rowid table, INTEGER PRIMARY KEY is special: supplying NULL allocates an integer key instead of storing NULL. That autoallocation does not apply to WITHOUT ROWID. These are distinctions, not a recommendation to use nullable identities. The project checks successful rows; the local error example below separately demonstrates the rejected write.
Optional practice: attempt to add Mira/Mon a second time to the first table. Identify both column names in the reported uniqueness failure.
after: A composite key is a key made from several columns. `PRIMARY KEY(person, day)` makes each person-and-day pair unique. The same person can have another day, and another person can use the same day.
Put NOT NULL on both columns so neither part is missing. Do not assume every ordinary SQLite primary-key declaration rejects missing values.

Run this example in a fresh database:
```sql
CREATE TABLE demo_slots (
  person TEXT NOT NULL,
  day TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY(person, day)
);
INSERT INTO demo_slots VALUES
  ('Lena', 'Mon'), ('Lena', 'Tue'), ('Noor', 'Mon');
SELECT person, day
FROM demo_slots
ORDER BY person, day;
```
All three pairs are different, so all three rows are accepted.

A UNIQUE rule can also forbid repeated complete pairs. But SQLite treats NULLs as different for uniqueness, so missing parts can allow rows that look repeated. Requiring both values avoids that problem here.
Adding Lena/Mon again would repeat the whole key and fail. Reusing only Lena or only Mon is allowed. Keep deliberate failures out of the normal project submission.
Create `slots` with required text columns `person` and `day`, using them together as the primary key. Store Mira/Mon, Mira/Tue, and Oren/Mon once each.
